headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 943 as 5 children die in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in measles-related deaths and symptoms across Bangladesh.
details: Five people died from measles symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) released Tuesday.
The deaths occurred between Monday 8 AM and Tuesday 8 AM, bringing the total number of deaths from measles symptoms to 844 since March 15.
Including 99 confirmed measles cases, the total death toll has reached 943. Four of the most recent deaths were in the Dhaka division and one was in the Sylhet division.
In the last 24 hours, 986 people showed measles symptoms nationwide. Since March 15, a total of 151,638 people have exhibited symptoms of the disease.
The DGHS also reported that 91 confirmed measles cases were identified in the last 24 hours, with total confirmed cases reaching 18,578 since March 15.
A total of 132,554 patients with measles symptoms have been hospitalized since March 15, of which 127,811 have been discharged after recovering.

headline: 88 deaths so far as 3 die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: Over 900 new patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in a single day, according to the Directorate General of Health Services.
details: Three people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a notification from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Tuesday.
During the same period, 907 new patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country.
The breakdown of new admissions shows 305 in Dhaka, 202 in Khulna, 163 in Barishal, 99 in Chattogram, 73 in Rajshahi, 45 in Mymensingh, 19 in Rangpur, and one in Sylhet.
Since January this year, the total number of dengue deaths has risen to 88.
A total of 30,830 people have been hospitalized for dengue treatment so far in 2024.
Currently, 2,090 dengue patients are receiving treatment in hospitals across Bangladesh.
